newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Bhutto may appear before U.S. jury if allowed.
newsitem.headline: Bhutto may appear before U.S. jury if allowed.

text.p: Former Pakistani prime minister Benazir Bhutto said on Monday she could appear before a U.S. jury in a fund-raising abuse case arising from the 1996 U.S. elections -- if the Pakistani government allows her to go.

Bhutto told a news conference on return home home from a private visit to the United States that the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) wanted to question her in connection with the case when she was there.
"I declined to be questioned," she said. "So they served me with subpoena...I was surprised."

A U.S. Justice Department task force probing fund-raising abuses during last year's election wants to question Bhutto about alleged efforts by Representative Dan Burton to pressure a lobbyist for her government to raise campaign contributions for him, the Washington Post reported on Saturday.

"I told the justice department that this is a matter between the U.S. government and the Pakistan government..," Bhutto said, adding that "if the Pakistan government gives a waiver, I will not obstruct the path of justice."
Bhutto was served with a subpoena earlier this week requiring her to appear before a federal grand jury hearing evidence in the investigation.
The jury is conducting a broad review of fund-raising practices in the Congressional and presidential elections, and has already questioned Mark Siegel, who was the lobbyist for Bhutto's government.
